title: Coordination, Review & Sign-Off

requirements.statement: Coordination activities shall be organized around distinct coordination stages or gates aligned to delivery milestones defined under S2.
All models subject to coordination shall be federated in a common, verified coordinate system before coordination checks are performed.
Coordination checks shall use defined check types, priorities, and tolerances documented in the project ruleset.
Coordination issues shall be uniquely identified, classified by priority and type, assigned to an identifiable responsible party, and tracked through a governed status progression.
A coordination sign-off shall be recorded at each governed coordination gate.
The Project BIM Manager, or delegated role per project RACI, shall hold approval authority for coordination sign-off.
Coordination check results, issue logs, and sign-off records shall be maintained as auditable evidence.
Unresolved coordination issues that cannot be resolved within the coordination cycle shall follow a defined escalation route.

A finding shall be treated as a governed coordination or compliance issue only when the applicable scope, governing expectation, due or milestone context, and authorized issue origin are explicitly identifiable.

Findings that do not satisfy issue-admissibility conditions shall not be reported as overdue obligations, compliance failures, or performance metrics; they shall remain observations or review feedback until governed conditions are met.
QA/QC evaluation shall first establish that the information is valid for evaluation in its current declared context, phase, and purpose before testing it against compliance expectations.

Continuous monitoring, expectation-based QA/QC, and milestone QA/QC shall be distinguished by purpose and consequence: continuous monitoring produces readiness signals, expectation-based QA/QC tests declared expectations, and milestone QA/QC supports governed issue, sign-off, or release decisions at declared gates.

QA/QC findings shall have consequence only within the reviewer's governed role, review scope, information state, and declared authority; findings outside those bounds shall remain observations pending appropriate governance action.

Dashboards, metrics, reports, or coordination views shall not create approval authority or redefine the governing status of underlying information; they are derived evidence and visibility mechanisms only.

implementation_boundary: This L4 standard is tool-agnostic. ACC, Navisworks, folder paths, export presets, numeric project tolerances, and issue-platform mechanics are implementation/project rules and are not elevated into enterprise doctrine.

provenance.migration_note: Machine-readable core reconciled with active narrative material and enriched from source issue-admissibility and contextual QA/QC doctrine. Source-specific organizational and contractual assertions were generalized; project-level authority remains governed by S1, BEP/RACI, and appointment context.
